newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt amends withholding tax arrangements.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt amends withholding tax arrangements.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday it would amend withholding tax arrangements in an effort to reduce compliance costs for small businesses.

Treasurer Peter Costello said changes to the pay-as-you-earn (PAYE), prescribed payments system (PPS) and the reportable payments system (RPS) would result in additional revenue of A$330 million in the 1998/99 financial year ending June 30.
"These modifications represent a significant first step towards simplifying the range of withholding tax systems imposed on business," Costello said in a statement.

Withholding tax is levied on income payments to Australians when they do not provide an investment body with a tax file number when making an investment, and on certain interest, dividend and royalty payments to foreigners.

Under the changes, the timing of payment of withheld amounts would be relaxed for a large number of small businesses, while the number of employers who remit tax installment deductions from employees on a quarterly basis would be extended.
"The option to remit quarterly, rather than monthly, will result in a reduction of paperwork and compliance costs for these small businesses," Costello said.

Payments by large withholders would be made earlier and under an electronic system, while the alignment of payment arrangements for other participants in PAYE, PPS and RPS would also reduce compliance costs.

The government said it expected withholding tax revenue to rise 9.8 percent in 1997/98 as a result of strong growth in collections of interest withholding tax and continued growth in dividend withholding tax.
